title: What Is Good Digital Citizenship?

source.name: VOA Learning English — What Is Good Digital Citizenship?
source.license: Nội dung của VOA (Voice of America), phạm vi công cộng
source.note: Đã rút gọn: chỉ giữ một số đoạn.

paras: Some adults and teachers may think young people want to spend all of their time using social media. But a recent survey shows that may not be true. It found that students sometimes want to turn off their electronic devices to get away from the pressure to take part in social media.
For the study, researchers led a series of discussions at classes in the United States. They asked young people what they thought about social media.

Eight out of ten students said that "some people think too much about their social media posts and are always trying to be perfect." About a third said it was acceptable “to post a version of yourself on social media that's not 100 percent real."

The students also talked about the issue of publishing unkind or hateful comments online. More than half of those questioned said that social media are "tearing us apart more than they are bringing people together."

Today, we will look at how teachers can support good digital citizenship through safe, kind and healthy use of social media. Common Sense Media defines digital citizenship as “thinking critically, behaving safely, and participating responsibly in the digital world.”
Teachers can begin by talking with students about how they use social media. How does it make them feel? Do the young people want to change anything about the way they interact with others online?
Teachers should learn what computer application programs their students use most often. Teachers should then use this information to keep in contact with students and share homework assignments.
Next, define the words cyberbullying , digital drama and hate speech. Young people need to recognize the differences among these issues and know how to deal with them.
“Digital drama” is the everyday arguments and small problems that come up between friends or with other people you know online or via text message.

“Hate speech” means expressing hatred of a particular group of people. For younger students, this is called ‘being mean.’ Teachers should let students know they are available to help when students face online problems.
Experts say teachers should choose a social media app their students often use. Limit posts or messages to once per class period or to what is necessary to provide information to students.

Bayly DiPilato is an English teacher and lives in New Jersey. She told National Public Radio that she did not want to use Facebook to communicate with students because it is too personal. Although her students have email, she found they do not often look at it.

DiPilato instead chose the social networking service Twitter to give out homework and reading materials. She says Twitter lets her share information quickly and show how to use social media in a professional, healthy way.

Experts also say teachers need to set time limits for using social media with students. Teachers could say they will only answer questions until nine at night on school nights, for example. They need to explain that adults, too, need to ‘unplug’ sometimes and get away from their phones and computers.

Part of digital citizenship is related to privacy. When sharing something done in class, teachers must remember to post pictures of students’ work but not of the students themselves. This is done to protect the online privacy of students.

Social media, electronics and digital resources are an increasingly large part of students’ lives. Experts say that with the guidance of teachers and other adults, young people can learn to become good digital citizens.

questions.q: What does the survey in the first paragraph suggest about young people?
options: They believe that social media brings friends closer than meeting in person
Some feel under pressure and would like a break from their devices
They think that teachers should forbid the use of social media in school
They would like to spend even more of their free time on social media
questions.explain: Đoạn 1: học sinh “sometimes want to turn off their electronic devices to get away from the pressure to take part in social media”.

questions.q: What do the results in paragraph 3 suggest?
options: Students see pressure to look perfect, and some accept an image that is not honest
A third of the students said that they had been bullied online
Eight out of ten students refuse to have an account of any kind
Most students post only completely honest information about their lives
questions.explain: Đoạn 3: 8/10 nói nhiều người “always trying to be perfect”; khoảng một phần ba cho rằng chấp nhận được việc đăng hình ảnh “not 100 percent real”.

questions.q: Which of the following would count as “digital drama”?
options: A class makes a poster about staying safe when using the internet
Two friends argue about something said in a group chat
A stranger posts comments full of hatred for a particular religious group
A teacher posts the homework instructions for the coming week
questions.explain: Đoạn 9: digital drama = tranh cãi thường ngày và vấn đề nhỏ giữa bạn bè qua mạng/tin nhắn. Đăng lời căm ghét một nhóm người là hate speech (đoạn 10).

questions.q: Why did Bayly DiPilato decide not to use Facebook with her students?
options: Her school had banned all teachers from using the site
She felt it was too personal for contact between teacher and class
She found it much too slow for sharing homework with a class
Her students were not old enough to open accounts on the site
questions.explain: Đoạn 12: cô không muốn dùng Facebook “because it is too personal”.

questions.q: What does DiPilato believe using Twitter allows her to do?
options: Avoid the need to set any limits on when she answers questions
Share information fast while showing a sensible, professional style of use
Keep a private record of every student’s marks and attendance
Replace the lessons in class with discussions held online
questions.explain: Đoạn 13: Twitter cho phép cô “share information quickly and show how to use social media in a professional, healthy way”.

questions.q: Why do experts suggest teachers say they will only answer questions until nine at night?
options: It encourages students to finish their homework earlier in the day
It shows students that adults also need time away from their screens
Students are not allowed to ask their teachers questions at night
The school computer network is switched off after that time every night
questions.explain: Đoạn 14: giáo viên cần đặt giới hạn thời gian và giải thích rằng “adults, too, need to ‘unplug’ sometimes”.

questions.q: Teachers are advised to post photos of students’ work rather than photos of the students themselves.
questions.explain: Đoạn 15: “post pictures of students’ work but not of the students themselves” để bảo vệ quyền riêng tư.

questions.q: Most teachers in the United States already use Twitter to give out homework.
questions.explain: Bài chỉ kể ví dụ một giáo viên (DiPilato); không nói có bao nhiêu giáo viên dùng Twitter.
